meta.name: Little Two
meta.blurb: A three-player climbing card game: shed singles, pairs, triples and runs over 3 deals; the lowest total penalty wins.

rules:
CARDS. There are {card_count_total} cards numbered 1 to {card_count_total}. A card's rank is (card + 2) divided by 3, rounded down, giving ranks 1 to {rank_count}. Its suit is card - 3 x (rank - 1), giving suits 1 to {suit_count}. For example card 14 has rank 5, suit 2. A higher card number always beats a lower one. Rank {two_rank} (cards {two_lowest_card}, 29, 30) are called 'twos'.

SEATS. The players sit as A (seat 1), B (seat 2) and C (seat 3). Turn order is always A, then B, then C, then A again.

MATCH. The match has {deals} deals and at most {max_orbits} orbits. An orbit is one turn for each seat in order.

DEALING. At the start of each deal, all {card_count_total} cards are shuffled. Each player is dealt {hand_size} cards, privately. The remaining {cards_aside} cards are set aside face-down; nobody sees them during the deal. Every player's card count is public at all times.

COMBINATIONS. There are four kinds:
- Single: one card.
- Pair: {pair_size} cards of the same rank.
- Triple: {triple_size} cards of the same rank.
- Run: {run_length} cards of three consecutive ranks, any suits. Ranks do not wrap around, so 9-10-1 is not a run.
The value of a combination is its highest card number. For example 4,5,6 is a triple of rank 2 and 4,5 is a pair of rank 2; 14,16 is not a pair.

THE PILE. The pile holds a current kind and a current value, or is empty.
- When the pile is empty, the player whose turn it is must lead any combination. They may not pass.
- When the pile is not empty, the player whose turn it is may pass, or may play a combination of the same kind with a higher value.
- Bomb: a triple may be played on a single or a pair whatever its value. The pile's kind then becomes triple.
- A triple on the pile can only be beaten by a higher triple.
- A run can only be beaten by a higher run.
Played cards are announced to everyone and removed from the game for the rest of the deal: they leave your hand, your card count drops by the number played, the pile value becomes the highest card and you become the last player. On your turn you are offered only the combinations you may legally play, written as card numbers (e.g. '13 14'), plus 'pass' when the pile is not empty.

PASSING AND CLEARING. A player who passes may play again the next time their turn comes in the same trick. The engine records who made the last play. If play comes back round to that player because both others passed since their play, the pile is cleared and that player must lead.

ILLEGAL PLAYS. An illegal or malformed play counts as a pass: the pile stays as it was. If the player was required to lead, their lowest-numbered card is played as a single instead. A legal play goes ahead as described above.

STARTING A DEAL. In deal 1, seat A leads first. In deal 2, seat B leads first. In deal 3, seat C leads first. Seats before the leader in the first orbit of a deal do not act in that orbit.

END OF A DEAL. A deal ends the moment a player plays their last card. That player wins the deal (deals won +1), and the rest of that orbit is skipped. The next deal begins at the start of the next orbit.

PENALTIES. Each non-winner receives a penalty equal to the number of cards left in their hand, plus {two_extra_penalty} for each two (rank {two_rank}) left in their hand; e.g. 3 cards including one two gives 4. If they have {double_threshold} or more cards left, this penalty is multiplied by {double_factor}; e.g. 7 cards with no twos gives 14. The deal winner receives {winner_penalty}. Penalties are added to each player's public running total.

END OF THE MATCH. The match ends after the third deal ends, or at the end of orbit {max_orbits}, whichever comes first. If orbit {max_orbits} ends during a deal, that deal is scored as if it had ended with no winner: every player receives a penalty under the rule above.

WINNING. The player with the lowest total penalty after the match ends wins. If two or three players tie for the lowest total, they share the result (a draw).
